newsitem.title: UK: TABLE TENNIS-NO PUNISHMENT FOR QATAR, ALGERIA AND IRAN.
newsitem.headline: TABLE TENNIS-NO PUNISHMENT FOR QATAR, ALGERIA AND IRAN.

text.p: The International Table Tennis Federation is not taking any disciplinary action against Qatar, Iran and Algeria for failing to play Israel in the team event at the world championships, a senior ITTF official said on Sunday.
The three Muslim nations fulfilled their fixtures against the other teams in their eight-nation group but did not show up for the Israeli matches.
The Israelis, who were awarded walkovers, lodged an official protest on April 29 calling for the teams and their players to be expelled from the championships.
ITTF's deputy president Adam Shira said the ITTF jury had met delegates from the three countries on May 2 and listened to their explanations why the matches had not gone ahead.

Qatar and Iran blamed travel problems, saying they arrived too late for the matches, while Algerian team leader Abdelkader Derkaoui told the jury he had arrived 15 minutes before the match was due and reported that two of his players were ill. He had produced two doctor's prescriptions as proof.

Derkaoui said Algeria had no objection to playing Israel. His team would be prepared to compete against them if a match was arranged but one of the players who lived in France would be leaving early next day.
Qatar also said they would play Israel and had competed against an Israeli team in the Bulgarian Open last year.

After examining the jury report, the ITTF's Chinese president Xu Yinsheng decided no further action was necessary. "The teams had all lost a match by default and there were three wins for Israel, so it was decided to let the matter rest," Shira said.

Shira said the Israelis wanted to play the matches, even though the competition was over. Both Qatar and Algeria confirmed they would play but the Iranians said they would have to receive approval from Iran before making any commitment.

Asked whether the ITTF believed Qatar, Algeria and Iran had acted from political motives, Shira said: "We have our suspicions but we have to accept the jury reports." Shira said although teams have signed a declaration to compete against any nation designated according to the draw, there were no specific sanctions contained in the rules.

"Possible sanctions are scratching teams from the competition, making them repay the hospitality they receive or even banning them from the next championships. But we have to have something concrete, especially if they are proved to be political actions."

Marian Gisaru, president of the Israeli Table Tennis Assocation, said he was very disappointed by the outcome. "We came here to play them, their actions were political. They simply didn't arrive. We sent in our protest four days agao and only today do we get an answer and it's not as satisfactory answer."
Israeli team manager Ahron Goldenerg was less diplomatic, sending a letter to the ITTF president protesting that no disciplinary action was taken.

"It is hard to believe a group of intelligent gentlemen who are sitting as an appeal committee believes the stories which are presented by the involved nations and the organising committee does not take any action against them," the letter said.
"They aren't even brave enough to declare that they cannot play because of political reasons against Israel but instead of this they told unbelievable stories which were accepted by you.
"We still demand that you take all the necessary steps, including sanctions against the teams."
